Otherwise the address runs to the next space or tab or to the end of the line, one run of spaces and tabs is skipped, and the rest of the line, verbatim, is the cell's content. Content that begins with `=` is a formula; anything else is a literal. A literal that is empty, or a cell nobody declared, is the number 0. A literal that matches an optional `-`, digits, and optionally a `.` and more digits is that number. A literal that is exactly one of the error tokens `#DIV/0!`, `#REF!`, `#VALUE!`, `#CYCLE!`, `#NAME?` and `#ERR!` is that error. Everything else is text.

A formula body holds numbers written as digits with an optional `.` and more digits and no sign and no exponent, cell addresses, ranges written `A1:B3`, the bare words `TRUE` and `FALSE`, function calls, parentheses, and the operators `^`, `*`, `/`, `+`, `-`, `=`, `<>`, `<`, `<=`, `>` and `>=`. Spaces and tabs may sit anywhere between tokens. Names are read case-insensitively. Precedence, loosest first, is the comparisons, then `+` and `-`, then `*` and `/`, then `^`, and then a leading `-` or `+`; the comparisons and the additive and multiplicative operators group to the left, `^` groups to the right, and a leading sign binds tighter than `^`, so `-2^2` is 4 and `2^3^2` is 512.
